Pose accuracy and physical validity of three docking scoring functions

The full analysis report, read from the tables in results/

show the code that produced this 
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import os

import pandas as pd

# The report reads only files in results/ and figures/. It recomputes nothing, so
# a number here and the same number in the README come from one file.
#
# project.conf is located by walking up from the working directory rather than
# taken as a quarto parameter. Quarto renders from the qmd's own directory in
# some versions and from the project root in others, and a report that cannot
# find its own config depending on how it was invoked is not reproducible.
# VGB_CONFIG overrides, for the case where the config lives somewhere else.
candidates = []
if os.environ.get("VGB_CONFIG"):
    candidates.append(Path(os.environ["VGB_CONFIG"]))
here = Path.cwd().resolve()
candidates += [here / "project.conf"] + [p / "project.conf" for p in here.parents]
conf_file = next((c for c in candidates if c.is_file()), None)
if conf_file is None:
    raise SystemExit("project.conf not found; run scripts/00_configure.sh first")

sys.path.insert(0, str((conf_file.parent / "scripts").resolve()))
import lib_vgb as L

conf = L.load_conf(conf_file)
RESULTS = Path(conf["RESULTS_DIR"])
FIGURES = Path(conf["FIGURES_DIR"])
LOGS = Path(conf["LOG_DIR"])
PASS_A = L.conf_float(conf, "RMSD_PASS", 2.0)
STRICT_A = L.conf_float(conf, "RMSD_STRICT", 1.0)


def load(rel, root=RESULTS):
    p = Path(root) / rel
    if not p.is_file():
        return pd.DataFrame()
    return pd.read_csv(p, sep="\t")


success = load("success_rates.tsv")
arms = load("arm_comparison.tsv")
rmsd = load("rmsd_distributions.tsv")
timing = load("timing_distributions.tsv")
waterfall = load("pb_failure_waterfall.tsv")
symmetry = load("symmetry_effect.tsv")
seeds = load("seed_variance.tsv")
excluded = load("excluded.tsv")
versions = load("environment/versions.tsv")
provenance = load("data_provenance.tsv")
counts = load("dataset_counts.tsv")
xsummary = load("crossdock_set_summary.tsv")
prep_rec = load("preparation/receptor_prep.tsv")
prep_lig = load("preparation/ligand_prep.tsv")
align = load("preparation/crossdock_align.tsv")
boxes = pd.read_csv(Path(conf["CONFIG_DIR"]) / "boxes.tsv", sep="\t") \
    if (Path(conf["CONFIG_DIR"]) / "boxes.tsv").is_file() else pd.DataFrame()

print(f"report built from {RESULTS}")
print(f"tables loaded: success={len(success)} arms={len(arms)} runs_scored="
      f"{len(load('scored/run_scores.tsv'))}")

What was measured

Three docking scoring functions were run on two published benchmark sets and on a cross-docking set built here, under five protocols that differ only in how much crystallographic information the search was given. Every pose was scored twice: once for how far it sits from the crystal pose, using a symmetry-corrected root-mean-square deviation, and once for whether it is physically possible, using the PoseBusters checks. The number this report calls success requires both.

A large gap between top-1 and top-5 means the search found the pose and the scoring function failed to rank it first. That is a different diagnosis from a small gap, and it has a different fix: rescoring the poses you already have, rather than searching harder.

How much of this is sampling noise

Every number above was produced at the docking programs’ own default search effort, which is also the setting the protocol these results are compared against uses. That default does not converge on a 25 Angstrom box, and the size of the resulting noise is a property of the standard protocol rather than of this pipeline.

show the code that produced this 
conv = load("convergence.tsv")
if not conv.empty:
    display(conv[["method", "exhaustiveness", "n_runs", "n_complexes",
                  "rmsd_le_2a_pct", "median_rmsd", "median_elapsed_s",
                  "complexes_where_seeds_disagree", "pct_seeds_disagree",
                  "mean_seed_range_a", "max_seed_range_a"]])
else:
    print("results/convergence.tsv is empty. Run:")
    print("  bash scripts/06_dock.sh --convergence --method vina")
results/convergence.tsv is empty. Run:
  bash scripts/06_dock.sh --convergence --method vina

The column to read is complexes_where_seeds_disagree: how many of the sampled complexes gave a different verdict at the 2 Angstrom line depending only on the random seed. At the default setting that number is not zero, which means a share of the difference between any two arms in this report is the search failing to converge rather than the information the arm withholds.

Two individual cases make the mechanism concrete, and they fail differently.

1HQ2_PH2 has one rotatable bond and a generated starting conformer already within 0.21 Angstrom of the crystal conformer, so there is almost nothing for the search to get wrong except where to put a nearly rigid body. At the default effort it returned a top-1 RMSD of 4.57 Angstrom on one seed and 0.33 Angstrom on another, with the receptor, the ligand, the box and the effort identical. At exhaustiveness 64 both seeds gave 0.37 Angstrom. That is a sampling failure and more search fixes it.

1GPK_HUP is huperzine A, which has no rotatable bonds at all. At every search effort tried and on both seeds, the correct pose was found and ranked second, at 0.36 to 0.39 Angstrom, while a pose 3.63 Angstrom away was ranked first. No amount of search fixes that: the scoring function prefers the wrong pose. Given the crystal coordinates as its starting point the same function ranks the right pose first, at 0.25 Angstrom, because the local optimiser never leaves it.

Both failures are invisible in the arm that starts from crystal coordinates, which is the arm the standard protocol reports.

The last column counts poses where two independent symmetry-corrected implementations, PoseBusters’ own and spyrmsd, differ by more than 0.1 Angstrom. Two libraries agreeing is weak evidence that either is right, but it is the cheapest evidence available, and a column of zeros is worth more than an assumption.

What the score is, and is not

Every docking program here reports a number in kcal per mole. It is the output of an empirical function whose coefficients were fitted to a training set of complexes with measured affinities. It is not a measured free energy of binding, it is not a calculated one, and the correlation between it and measured affinity across unrelated targets is poor enough that ranking two different molecules by it is not supported. This report uses the score for one purpose only, which is to decide which of a run’s poses is the top-ranked one. Nothing here measures affinity.
